sources.title: Tomasz Kochanek, Functional analysis, Lecture 1 (complete five-page lecture notes)
sources.locator: Complete five-page Lecture 1 read from the retained PDF and extracted text. Printed pp. 1-3, Definition 1.1: norm axioms over K=R or C; pp. 1-3, Example 1.2: finite coordinate norms including the complex p=1 sum; p. 4, Definition 1.5: equivalence by positive real constants.

contents.name: Definition 1.1: real- and complex-vector-space norm axioms with absolute homogeneity for every scalar in K
Example 1.2(1): finite coordinate p-norms over K, including the sum of coordinate moduli when p=1
Definition 1.5: equivalent norms are bounded in both directions by positive constants
The lecture's broader normed-space examples and Riesz lemma
contents.reason: They do not supply a claim in this six-item A inventory; no theorem about finite-dimensional norm equivalence or realification is imported from them.

sources.title: M. Winklmeier, Functional Analysis lecture notes (complete 140-page lecture notes)
sources.locator: Complete 140-page lecture-notes PDF. Chapter 1 §1.2, Definition 1.10 (printed p. 11): norm on a vector space over K with K=R or C; Example 1.15(i) (p. 13): coordinate p-norms on C^n and R^n; Definition 1.17 and Theorem 1.18 (p. 17): equivalent norms and the full convergence argument.

contents.name: Definition 1.10: norm on a vector space over K=R or C, including complex absolute homogeneity
Example 1.15(i): coordinate p-norms on C^n and R^n; the local proof separately treats n=0
Definition 1.17: equivalence via positive constants bounding one norm by the other
Theorem 1.18: the convergence characterization of equivalent norms and its proof
contents.reason: This batch defines equivalence but does not claim the topology or convergence characterization.
